I wrote the research note to `/tmp/work/research.json`, with all six claims (C1–C6) answered. It uses only the supplied Python 3.13.0 `asyncio-task.rst` extract, cited by original line numbers (lines 290–416 and 508–599). I did no web search.

- **Failed child:** `TaskGroup` cancels the remaining siblings when a child fails. `gather` with the default `return_exceptions=False` raises the first exception but leaves the other awaitables running.
- **What each waits for:** the `TaskGroup` `async with` waits for all tasks, including ones added while it waits. `gather` returns an ordered list of results on success and stops at the first exception by default.
- **Grouped exceptions:** `TaskGroup` raises an `ExceptionGroup` or `BaseExceptionGroup`. `KeyboardInterrupt` and `SystemExit` are re-raised on their own instead, and `CancelledError` is left out of the group.
- **Cancelled child in `gather`:** it counts as if it raised `CancelledError`, and the `gather()` call itself is not cancelled. Cancelling `gather()` itself does cancel the children that haven't finished.
- **Swallowing `CancelledError`:** `TaskGroup` and `asyncio.timeout()` use cancellation internally and may misbehave if it is swallowed. If suppressing it is truly needed, `uncancel()` must also be called.
- **Recommendation:** use `TaskGroup` for all-or-cancel sibling work. It needs Python 3.11 or later, and the 3.13 docs describe improved cancellation handling.

**Unverified in the docs:**
- The extract doesn't say that `gather` waits for every awaitable when `return_exceptions=True`.
- It doesn't say how a cancelled child is surfaced to the caller of `gather`.
- It doesn't list concrete failure modes of swallowing `CancelledError`.
- `ExceptionGroup` and `except*` availability by version isn't covered.
- The 3.10 `gather` note is cut off.

I listed these as unknowns in the note.

7	00293 | 
8	00294 | Task Cancellation
9	00295 | =================
10	00296 | 
11	00297 | Tasks can easily and safely be cancelled.
12	00298 | When a task is cancelled, :exc:`asyncio.CancelledError` will be raised
13	00299 | in the task at the next opportunity.
14	00300 | 
15	00301 | It is recommended that coroutines use ``try/finally`` blocks to robustly
16	00302 | perform clean-up logic. In case :exc:`asyncio.CancelledError`
17	00303 | is explicitly caught, it should generally be propagated when
18	00304 | clean-up is complete. :exc:`asyncio.CancelledError` directly subclasses
19	00305 | :exc:`BaseException` so most code will not need to be aware of it.
20	00306 | 
21	00307 | The asyncio components that enable structured concurrency, like
22	00308 | :class:`asyncio.TaskGroup` and :func:`asyncio.timeout`,
23	00309 | are implemented using cancellation internally and might misbehave if
24	00310 | a coroutine swallows :exc:`asyncio.CancelledError`. Similarly, user code
25	00311 | should not generally call :meth:`uncancel <asyncio.Task.uncancel>`.
26	00312 | However, in cases when suppressing :exc:`asyncio.CancelledError` is
27	00313 | truly desired, it is necessary to also call ``uncancel()`` to completely
28	00314 | remove the cancellation state.
29	00315 | 
30	00316 | .. _taskgroups:
31	00317 | 
32	00318 | Task Groups
33	00319 | ===========
34	00320 | 
35	00321 | Task groups combine a task creation API with a convenient
36	00322 | and reliable way to wait for all tasks in the group to finish.
37	00323 | 
38	00324 | .. class:: TaskGroup()
39	00325 | 
40	00326 |    An :ref:`asynchronous context manager <async-context-managers>`
41	00327 |    holding a group of tasks.
42	00328 |    Tasks can be added to the group using :meth:`create_task`.
43	00329 |    All tasks are awaited when the context manager exits.
44	00330 | 
45	00331 |    .. versionadded:: 3.11
46	00332 | 
47	00333 |    .. method:: create_task(coro, *, name=None, context=None)
48	00334 | 
49	00335 |       Create a task in this task group.
50	00336 |       The signature matches that of :func:`asyncio.create_task`.
51	00337 |       If the task group is inactive (e.g. not yet entered,
52	00338 |       already finished, or in the process of shutting down),
53	00339 |       we will close the given ``coro``.
54	00340 | 
55	00341 |       .. versionchanged:: 3.13
56	00342 | 
57	00343 |          Close the given coroutine if the task group is not active.
58	00344 | 
59	00345 | Example::
60	00346 | 
61	00347 |     async def main():
62	00348 |         async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as tg:
63	00349 |             task1 = tg.create_task(some_coro(...))
64	00350 |             task2 = tg.create_task(another_coro(...))
65	00351 |         print(f"Both tasks have completed now: {task1.result()}, {task2.result()}")
66	00352 | 
67	00353 | The ``async with`` statement will wait for all tasks in the group to finish.
68	00354 | While waiting, new tasks may still be added to the group
69	00355 | (for example, by passing ``tg`` into one of the coroutines
70	00356 | and calling ``tg.create_task()`` in that coroutine).
71	00357 | Once the last task has finished and the ``async with`` block is exited,
72	00358 | no new tasks may be added to the group.
73	00359 | 
74	00360 | The first time any of the tasks belonging to the group fails
75	00361 | with an exception other than :exc:`asyncio.CancelledError`,
76	00362 | the remaining tasks in the group are cancelled.
77	00363 | No further tasks can then be added to the group.
78	00364 | At this point, if the body of the ``async with`` statement is still active
79	00365 | (i.e., :meth:`~object.__aexit__` hasn't been called yet),
80	00366 | the task directly containing the ``async with`` statement is also cancelled.
81	00367 | The resulting :exc:`asyncio.CancelledError` will interrupt an ``await``,
82	00368 | but it will not bubble out of the containing ``async with`` statement.
83	00369 | 
84	00370 | Once all tasks have finished, if any tasks have failed
85	00371 | with an exception other than :exc:`asyncio.CancelledError`,
86	00372 | those exceptions are combined in an
87	00373 | :exc:`ExceptionGroup` or :exc:`BaseExceptionGroup`
88	00374 | (as appropriate; see their documentation)
89	00375 | which is then raised.
90	00376 | 
91	00377 | Two base exceptions are treated specially:
92	00378 | If any task fails with :exc:`KeyboardInterrupt` or :exc:`SystemExit`,
93	00379 | the task group still cancels the remaining tasks and waits for them,
94	00380 | but then the initial :exc:`KeyboardInterrupt` or :exc:`SystemExit`
95	00381 | is re-raised instead of :exc:`ExceptionGroup` or :exc:`BaseExceptionGroup`.
96	00382 | 
97	00383 | If the body of the ``async with`` statement exits with an exception
98	00384 | (so :meth:`~object.__aexit__` is called with an exception set),
99	00385 | this is treated the same as if one of the tasks failed:
100	00386 | the remaining tasks are cancelled and then waited for,
101	00387 | and non-cancellation exceptions are grouped into an
102	00388 | exception group and raised.
103	00389 | The exception passed into :meth:`~object.__aexit__`,
104	00390 | unless it is :exc:`asyncio.CancelledError`,
105	00391 | is also included in the exception group.
106	00392 | The same special case is made for
107	00393 | :exc:`KeyboardInterrupt` and :exc:`SystemExit` as in the previous paragraph.
108	00394 | 
109	00395 | Task groups are careful not to mix up the internal cancellation used to
110	00396 | "wake up" their :meth:`~object.__aexit__` with cancellation requests
111	00397 | for the task in which they are running made by other parties.
112	00398 | In particular, when one task group is syntactically nested in another,
113	00399 | and both experience an exception in one of their child tasks simultaneously,
114	00400 | the inner task group will process its exceptions, and then the outer task group
115	00401 | will receive another cancellation and process its own exceptions.
116	00402 | 
117	00403 | In the case where a task group is cancelled externally and also must
118	00404 | raise an :exc:`ExceptionGroup`, it will call the parent task's
119	00405 | :meth:`~asyncio.Task.cancel` method. This ensures that a
120	00406 | :exc:`asyncio.CancelledError` will be raised at the next
121	00407 | :keyword:`await`, so the cancellation is not lost.
122	00408 | 
123	00409 | Task groups preserve the cancellation count
124	00410 | reported by :meth:`asyncio.Task.cancelling`.
125	00411 | 
126	00412 | .. versionchanged:: 3.13
127	00413 | 
128	00414 |    Improved handling of simultaneous internal and external cancellations
129	00415 |    and correct preservation of cancellation counts.
130	00416 |

132	00508 | Running Tasks Concurrently
133	00509 | ==========================
134	00510 | 
135	00511 | .. awaitablefunction:: gather(*aws, return_exceptions=False)
136	00512 | 
137	00513 |    Run :ref:`awaitable objects <asyncio-awaitables>` in the *aws*
138	00514 |    sequence *concurrently*.
139	00515 | 
140	00516 |    If any awaitable in *aws* is a coroutine, it is automatically
141	00517 |    scheduled as a Task.
142	00518 | 
143	00519 |    If all awaitables are completed successfully, the result is an
144	00520 |    aggregate list of returned values.  The order of result values
145	00521 |    corresponds to the order of awaitables in *aws*.
146	00522 | 
147	00523 |    If *return_exceptions* is ``False`` (default), the first
148	00524 |    raised exception is immediately propagated to the task that
149	00525 |    awaits on ``gather()``.  Other awaitables in the *aws* sequence
150	00526 |    **won't be cancelled** and will continue to run.
151	00527 | 
152	00528 |    If *return_exceptions* is ``True``, exceptions are treated the
153	00529 |    same as successful results, and aggregated in the result list.
154	00530 | 
155	00531 |    If ``gather()`` is *cancelled*, all submitted awaitables
156	00532 |    (that have not completed yet) are also *cancelled*.
157	00533 | 
158	00534 |    If any Task or Future from the *aws* sequence is *cancelled*, it is
159	00535 |    treated as if it raised :exc:`CancelledError` -- the ``gather()``
160	00536 |    call is **not** cancelled in this case.  This is to prevent the
161	00537 |    cancellation of one submitted Task/Future to cause other
162	00538 |    Tasks/Futures to be cancelled.
163	00539 | 
164	00540 |    .. note::
165	00541 |       A new alternative to create and run tasks concurrently and
166	00542 |       wait for their completion is :class:`asyncio.TaskGroup`. *TaskGroup*
167	00543 |       provides stronger safety guarantees than *gather* for scheduling a nesting of subtasks:
168	00544 |       if a task (or a subtask, a task scheduled by a task)
169	00545 |       raises an exception, *TaskGroup* will, while *gather* will not,
170	00546 |       cancel the remaining scheduled tasks).
171	00547 | 
172	00548 |    .. _asyncio_example_gather:
173	00549 | 
174	00550 |    Example::

176	00552 |       import asyncio
177	00553 | 
178	00554 |       async def factorial(name, number):
179	00555 |           f = 1
180	00556 |           for i in range(2, number + 1):
181	00557 |               print(f"Task {name}: Compute factorial({number}), currently i={i}...")

188	00564 |           # Schedule three calls *concurrently*:
